title: ou says /ow/
parentNote: ou says /ow/ — the noise you make when you stub a toe. loud, shout, found, cloud, ground. This is a brand new sound, not another spelling of something we have already done, and that is worth saying out loud because it looks so much like a team we met three days ago. ow still says /oh/ (snow, blow, grow) and it will keep saying /oh/ for a long time yet; today's sound belongs to ou and only ou. The slip to expect is the two getting swapped, so loud comes out as lohd, or snow comes out with an ouch in it. Keep a snow word and a loud word side by side on the sofa and point at whichever one they need. Nothing else about ou changes: it sits in the middle or at the front, two letters, one sound, and the u never speaks on its own.

activities.mouthCue: Your mouth drops wide open and then squeezes small and round, all in one go: ow.
activities.prompt: A brand new sound. Two letters, and the u does not speak on its own: ou.

activities.title: The loud sound in the shed
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: Meg and I sat outside on the ground and did munch hot toast.
Then the shed did let out a loud sound. Bang! Bang!
I did drop the toast. The sound did not stop.
It did sound like a drum bumping round and round.
Meg is not the sort to stand and wait, and I am.
Meg did creep up to the shed and did lift the flap.
Out did dash a fat red hen, and it did land on the ground.
It had found a tin tub, and it did stamp in it. Bang! Bang!
Meg did grin. The drum is a hen, and the hen is proud.
I did pick up the toast. The hen did want it, but I did not let it.
